prompt:
(a) Explain what is meant by energy dissipation. [1]
(b) Name the primary form into which mechanical energy is dissipated when two surfaces slide against each other. [1]
answer:
(a) The transformation of energy into non-useful / degraded forms that spread out into the surroundings and cannot be fully recovered.
(b) Internal thermal energy (heat).

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) energy spreading out / transferring into non-useful (or degraded / less concentrated) forms
(b) internal thermal energy (allow heat / thermal energy)

hints: In (a), think about how energy spreads out and whether it remains available for useful work.
In (b), consider the microscopic consequence of friction between sliding surfaces.
solution:
(a) Energy dissipation refers to the process by which input energy is converted into non-useful forms (primarily thermal energy) that spread out into the surroundings, making it unavailable to do useful mechanical work.
(b) Friction converts mechanical energy primarily into internal thermal energy (heat) in the contacting bodies and surrounding air.
teacher_walkthrough: Emphasize that dissipated energy is not destroyed; it is simply degraded and dispersed.
In part (b), internal thermal energy is the preferred Cambridge terminology.
